correctness.rationale: The transition-matrix in-degree telescoping identity is proved exactly. Its b-terms are cyclic adjacent differences at positions bounded by each suffix length, since a short suffix maps (0,1) to the same point or to a consecutive pair indexed by its number of a letters. The first positive boundary gives the strict lower bound, and ba^r realizes +1. Every other word of this length has no positive contribution, proving unique optimality. Prefix decomposition 1^h0^(d-h)1 with free remaining bits proves refined and unrefined counts, exceptional n-1 sets, and the mean. The independent finite BFS and explicit word enumeration reproduced the theorem for n=3..11 and n=3..9 respectively. Enumeration is not used to infer arbitrary n.

value.rationale: Subset-specific shortest extending words are essential primitives in the extension method for synchronizing automata. The classical Černý family is an extremal benchmark explicitly singled out in the recent source as violating a uniform n-1 threshold. Determining exactly which n-1 subsets are obstructions, with the unique optimal word for every subset and an all-sizes histogram, directly quantifies this obstruction; the average tending to 3 while the maximum equals n is a structural contrast not supplied by general certificates, avoidance bounds, or reset lengths. It is a complete natural infinite-family classification, not an arbitrary finite instance.
